title: Carts, grabbing and the physics of loot
summary: R.E.P.O.'s loot is physical: the game gives a cart its own physics, objects you can grab that do not move, and monsters that are physical objects too.
body: Movement is part of the challenge rather than a menu action: the game models a cart with its own physical behaviour, so pushing one is a decision you make with your hands.
Some objects are meant to be grabbed without moving, which is why the game separates a fixed grab target from loose loot.
A fixed grab target carries its own details: the collider you actually touch, the spot its prompt sits at on screen, the words that prompt shows, and whether a player has hold of it.
Monsters are physical too, so contact with them is a collision rather than a scripted event.
What this entry does not tell you: how much a cart holds, how heavy anything is or how hard a monster hits. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A cart is modelled with its own physical behaviour.
The game defines objects that can be grabbed but do not move.
Monsters are physical objects in the game.
A monster exists whose job is to throw something at your valuables.
A fixed grab target carries its own collider, the spot its prompt sits at, the words it shows, and whether a player is holding it.

facts.claim: The claw a player grabs with is named in the build, with a left and a right mesh of its own.
